set.acceptance_criteria: TR-001's escalation states who clears a condition when its sponsor is gone; if a successor may clear it, the validator accepts that and a test covers it; section 10 scores more than 80 with 0 blocking defects.
set.body: Only the approver who set a condition may clear it. Nothing says what happens when that sponsor leaves before every condition is cleared, so the set can stay approved with conditions forever. Found by the grade of section 10 at 0.12.0.
set.title: PRD: say who clears a condition when the sponsor who set it is gone

set.acceptance_criteria: PER-002's external flag, population, and body text match the decision; sections 2 and 4 agree; section 4 scores more than 80 with 0 blocking defects.
set.body: Section 4 says no persona is external, but section 2 quotes a partner who hands the PRD to the client's engineers. If the client's engineer judges buildability, PER-002 is external. Found by the grade of section 4 at 0.12.0.
set.title: PRD: decide whether PER-002, the engineering lead, is external

set.acceptance_criteria: NFR-001's target and note agree; NFR-001 has a source; section 8 scores more than 80 with 0 blocking defects.
set.body: NFR-001 allows a 20-second wait at p95, but its own note says 20 seconds across 60 questions makes the expert stop. No NFR has a source. Found by the grade of section 8 at 0.12.0.
set.title: PRD: reconcile NFR-001's 20-second target with its own rationale

set.acceptance_criteria: bin/worklog runs, worklog doctor passes, and the three grading findings are worklog items linked to GitHub issues #25, #26, and #27.
set.body: Scaffold the worklog in this repository, so plans and tickets live in git and sync to GitHub Issues and the GitHub wiki.
set.title: Set up the WikiTicket worklog for prd-forge

set.acceptance_criteria: From a PRD document the pane opens the backlog item derived from it, and from a backlog item it opens the PRD item it traces to; a slash command or link works in both directions; tests cover both directions.
set.body: A user moves from the PRD set to the backlog that prd-to-backlog derives, and back, without losing context. Covers the /prd pane and the terminal display in this plugin. The prd-forge-viewer desktop app has its own issue.
set.title: Navigate both ways between the PRD and its backlog

set.acceptance_criteria: An FAQ page exists and the README links to it; it compares grading, review agents, validation, requirement tests, output, and backlog tracing, and names the shared concepts; every claim about prd-forge matches the code.
set.body: Add an FAQ, linked from the README, that answers why to use prd-forge instead of Anthropic's product-management plugin for a classical PRD.
set.title: FAQ: why prd-forge over Anthropic's product-management plugin

set.acceptance_criteria: The four acceptance criteria in issue 24 section 10 pass, and its open questions are decided.
set.body: A roadmap saved as a file in the PRD set: items with an RM id, a horizon, a status, and links to releases and objectives, with scoring, dependencies, a rubric, validator rules, a diagram, and a /prd-roadmap command. Design spec in issue 24.
set.title: Roadmap support: a roadmap document kind with /prd-roadmap
